fact_check_log.claim: Key takeaway 3 / FAQ: Notice of Intended Marriage to an authorised celebrant at least 1 month and no more than 18 months before the wedding
As at November 2026, Marriage Act 1961 and Marriage Regulations 2017 set the rules; general information, not legal advice
NOIM reaches celebrant 1 to 18 months ahead; can be completed while overseas (edit 13 aligns wording to AGD 'if you are overseas')
Less than 1 month away: talk to celebrant; prescribed authority may approve
Authorised celebrant must perform the ceremony; four types listed
AGD register of Commonwealth-registered celebrants, searchable by name and filterable by state
3 certificates signed by couple, celebrant and 2 witnesses over 18; day certificate is ceremonial; celebrant submits to state or territory registry within 14 days
Whitsundays: BoM records for an island airport show January and February far wetter, with many more rain days, than late winter and early spring (no figures quoted)
'On an island in the Whitsundays, summer brings the wet months' (season interpretation, December not in fact_06; page has no season summary)
'A reef island and a southern vineyard can sit in very different weather in the same month' (no BoM source)
Sun protection once UV reaches 3 or above; UV cannot be seen or felt; check UV on SunSmart app or BoM website ('forecast' corrected to UV level in edit 16)
Shade reduces UV but reflection still reaches you; combine with clothing, hats, sunglasses, SPF 50 or SPF50+
Sunscreen at least 20 minutes before going out; reapply every two hours or after swimming or heavy sweating (sentence cut at panel stage; fact_09 no longer used, no marker in 08-final.md)
